solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Deficiency in rebuilt base where part of Russian navy is

definitions.text: where part of Russian navy is

indicators.note: the shortfall word sits inside the reworked letters of base
something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so the letters of base are rearranged

parts.note: the word base itself supplies the letters to be rearranged
a deficiency is a lack of something

explanation.surface: A shortage of something in a reconstructed military base where some Russian ships are stationed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: Russia's Black Sea Fleet is based at Sevastopol.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia keeps its Black Sea Fleet in that inland sea, so it is a place where part of its naval force lies.

clue.text: Author that is initially holding up American volume for book-lovers

indicators.note: in a down answer the upper piece holds up whatever is written beneath it, so the volume comes first

parts.note: the US spelling of the metric unit of volume

indicators.note: initially means taking the opening letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A writer seems to be delaying an American book in a way that matters to keen readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author' looks like the definition but supplies only its first letter; 'volume' looks like a book but is a measure of capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are the well-read, educated class who love literature and books.

clue.text: Fictional characters disturbed about study meant to be secret

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the room word, so they sit about it
letters disturbed are thrown out of their order, so the characters of fictional are rearranged

parts.note: the letters making up the word fictional
a den is a private study or workroom

explanation.surface: Characters in a novel are upset about a study that was supposed to stay hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' reads as people in a story but means the letters of the word fictional.
explanation.definitionFit: Something confidential is private information intended to be kept from others.

clue.text: Tyrant giving bad mark, with learner kept in

indicators.note: the learner letter is held inside the blemish word, kept in like a pupil after school

parts.note: a stain is a dirty mark or blemish

explanation.surface: A despot hands out poor grades and gives a pupil detention.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates on a British learner driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin, the Soviet dictator, is a byword for a ruthless despot.

clue.text: Ignoring origins of law, try being crooked

indicators.note: ignoring origins means each of the two words loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Advice to anyone tempted to bend the law and cheat their way through.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first letters of LAW and TRY leaves AW and RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means askew or out of line, which is a synonym of bent out of true.

clue.text: Details of course of naval vessel mate's heading North

indicators.note: in a down answer going north means reading upwards, so the whole piece is reversed

parts.note: sub is short for submarine
an ally is a mate or friend, with the possessive s kept

explanation.surface: Particulars of the route of a warship whose first officer is steering north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' sounds nautical alongside the vessel, but it is a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is the outline of topics covered in a course of study.

clue.text: Transformed prince, perhaps, changed for good

indicators.note: changed letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale prince who has been altered permanently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For good' looks like 'permanently' but splits into a word and the abbreviation G.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale a prince is turned into a frog by a spell, so a frog may be such an enchanted royal.

clue.text: Drop in financial support — it's not on the level

indicators.note: the falling word sits inside the funding word

parts.note: a grant is money given in support
to drop, as in drop dead, is to die

explanation.surface: A cut in funding is described as dishonest dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on the level' suggests dishonesty but literally means not flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope, something inclined rather than horizontal.

clue.text: How the scales of justice should operate better, we hear, for traveller

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is spoken and the entry is what it sounds like

parts.words: How the scales of justice should operate better
parts.note: scales weigh, and fairer means better in the sense of more just, so the phrase gives weigh fairer

explanation.surface: A wish that the scales of justice would weigh things more fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weigh fairer' spoken in a British accent matches the traveller's word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone journeying on foot, an old word for a wanderer on the road.

clue.text: Player as viewed by opponent in bridge school

parts.note: East is one of the four players at a bridge table
to, as in 'to me it looks fine', means in the view of
North sits beside East and plays against them

explanation.surface: A description of a card player from an opponent's seat at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points, N, E, S and W, with North-South against East-West.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Ready to get off the ground, completely developed

definitions.text: Ready to get off the ground
definitions.meaning: first meaning: of a young bird with all its feathers, able to fly
second meaning: fully trained or mature in a role

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from the same word: a fledged bird has its flight feathers, and the figurative sense is having reached full status.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird with grown flight feathers can fly, and by extension a person who has finished training is a full member.

clue.text: I had turned up poet's work showing more variety

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up means reading the short form from bottom to top

parts.note: the contraction I'd
versifying is writing verse

explanation.surface: Someone discovers the poems they have written are becoming more varied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like 'appeared' but asks for the contraction to be read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Diversifying means becoming more varied, branching into a wider range.

clue.text: Duke and I taken in by lustful churchman

indicators.note: the two short pieces are swallowed by the word for lustful

parts.note: carnal means of the flesh, sensual
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman and the speaker are deceived by a lecherous cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' reads as fooled but tells us to put the pieces inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal is a senior Roman Catholic prelate, a high-ranking man of the Church.

clue.text: Movement that's slowly taken inside popular government

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters spanning the two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of popular and the start of government

explanation.surface: Political change that comes about gradually under a populist regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' is political in the surface, but it is a section of a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction for a very slow tempo, and also a movement played at that pace.

clue.text: Black sheep's description — dull and stupid

parts.note: ovine means relating to sheep

explanation.surface: The family black sheep is written off as boring and dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black sheep' reads as one phrase but splits into the letter B and an adjective for sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Bovine literally means cow-like and is used figuratively of a slow, sluggish, unintelligent person.

clue.text: European hero of American novel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a native of Finland
second meaning: Huckleberry ..., Mark Twain's title character

explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is someone from Finland, and Huck Finn is the boy narrator of Twain's classic book.

clue.text: Border for skirt or winter coat further down

parts.note: an animal's fur is its thick coat for cold weather
below means lower down

explanation.surface: Choosing between a hem trim and a coat that comes lower for winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A furbelow is a pleated or gathered flounce trimming the edge of a dress or petticoat.

clue.text: Indian garments from South, having come to be cut

indicators.note: cutting the end letter off the word for come to be

parts.note: to arise is to come into being

explanation.surface: Clothes brought up from the south of India, later shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is the long draped wrap worn by women in India, so these are several such dresses.

clue.text: Inviolability of court, within reason

indicators.note: the court abbreviation is placed within the reason word

parts.note: reason as in losing one's reason, that is sanity

explanation.surface: A legal point about the court's untouchable status staying within reasonable bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reason' looks like logic but is mental soundness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctity is sacredness, the quality of being too holy or important to violate.

clue.text: Small part of litter, in turn, recycled

indicators.note: recycled material is processed into new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word turn itself supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Bits of rubbish taking their turn to be recycled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' suggests rubbish beside 'recycled', but it is a brood of young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The runt is the smallest, weakest animal born in a litter.

clue.text: Denial, for example, that's accepted by people

indicators.note: the example abbreviation is taken into the people word

parts.note: a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A refusal, for instance, that the public goes along with.
explanation.definitionFit: Negation is the act of contradicting or denying something.

clue.text: Quit or accept new contract?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to give up a job

explanation.walkthrough: The opposite senses come from one spelling: resign, and re-sign with a hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: Resigning means leaving one's post, while re-signing means renewing an agreement for another term.

clue.text: 15 joining game that brings rival universities together

indicators.note: the animal from 15 is joined to the card game, side by side

parts.note: the answer to 15 across is bovine, and an ox is a bovine animal
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A cow joins a game of cards that unites competing colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 15 gives an adjective; here it stands for an animal so described.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxbridge is a blend naming Oxford and Cambridge, the old rival English universities, as a pair.

clue.text: Attend one opening in theatre and quickly leave

parts.note: to attend is to be at an event

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only the first letter of theatre is used

explanation.surface: Go to the premiere at the playhouse, then slip away fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' suggests a first night but simply means first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is slang for go away at once, as in an order to clear off.

clue.text: Gradually developing as rebel after monarch's ousted as leader

indicators.note: the king letter is thrown out from the front of the rebel word

parts.note: a revolutionary is a rebel
R stands for Rex or Regina, Latin for king or queen, the letter removed from the front

explanation.surface: A rebel slowly gains ground after the king is overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: R is Rex, Latin for king.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolutionary describes change happening by slow, steady stages.

clue.text: Covering or partly covering

indicators.note: only part of the second clue word is used

parts.note: the word covering again, with its middle four letters taken

explanation.surface: A quibble over whether something hides an object entirely or only in part.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the fodder are the same word, a deliberate repeat by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Over describes something placed on top of or across another, as a cover.

clue.text: Gemstone seen in ring partner has on

indicators.note: in a down answer the partner carries the ring on top, so it comes first

parts.note: a pal is a friend or mate

explanation.surface: A jewel visible in the ring one's partner is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: O resembles a ring in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a precious stone with shifting rainbow colours.

clue.text: Island after island found in river

indicators.note: one island piece comes after the other

parts.note: the same short form for island again

explanation.surface: Islands strung one after another in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: IS is a standard abbreviation for island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isis is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford.

clue.text: Patience, for example, to repeat after revision

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: Patience is needed to repeat something after revising it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patience' looks like a virtue but is the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is a light comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, an example of the form.

clue.text: Person involved in case originally tailing leader of thieves

indicators.note: the letters as they were originally are now changed, a rearrangement

parts.note: the word tailing itself supplies the letters

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only the first letter of thieves is used

explanation.surface: A detective originally following a gang boss, which is how he got involved in the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a detective story but is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigant is a party to a lawsuit, someone suing or being sued.
